overview: Gwithian beach is part of the long, golden run of sand along St Ives Bay, backed by the high dunes of Gwithian Towans, about three miles north-east of Hayle. It faces west into the Atlantic, so it picks up the swell, and on a clear day you can see right across the bay to St Ives.
The dunes hide a surprising amount of history: a Bronze Age farm and the remains of an early chapel have been found under the sand, though there’s nothing to see of them today.

expect.title: Big beach, big skies
expect.text: A wide, open beach with lots of space and the dunes behind.

expect.title: Surf
expect.text: Facing west into the Atlantic, it’s popular with surfers.

expect.title: The village
expect.text: Gwithian village has a pub, the Red River Inn, named after the nearby river once stained red by mine waste.

goodToKnow.label: Where it is
goodToKnow.text: About three miles north-east of Hayle and four miles across the bay from St Ives.

week.text: Gwithian is a great beach for a long walk and a surf, and it’s easy to combine with Godrevy at the northern end. It faces west, so stay for the sunset.

pairWith.why: the lighthouse end of the bay

tips: Walk north along the sand towards Godrevy for the lighthouse view.
